scope: The identity observer distinguishes a SORTENTSTABLE object's outer self handle from group-5 sort keys after the host AcDbSortentsTable subclass marker. Application, XDATA and embedded boundaries retain priority. SortOrder is an appended public scope value and remains unknown to the existing namespace audit.

authority.title: Autodesk SORTENTSTABLE DXF group codes
authority.role: Distinguishes object handle group 5 from repeated subclass sort-handle group 5 associated with entity references.

originalObservation.provenance: Independent repository sample; native authoring history not independently certified.
originalObservation.census: Complete; 995 records, 1003 candidates, zero unmatched admissions. Original object 355 outer group 5 at byte 379916 remains Outer/Accepted, with one repeated same-scalar registration. Eight keys 35A, 354, 36E, 36D, 371, 370, 376 and 375 at bytes 380002 through 380114 are SortOrder/Unobserved; adjacent object identities 79B and A0D remain Outer/Accepted.
originalObservation.before: All eight sort keys were classified Outer/Unobserved, producing a false multiple-self identity record.

bindings.chronology: Final normal and ASan cohort included simultaneous legacy TABLE source-context changes committed as 1120c831, before SORTENTSTABLE commit c0a17266.

validation.controls: Four locally authored AC1018/AC1032 ASCII/binary import routes verify typed sort pairs, payload values equal to the object's own handle and to a later entity identity, app/XDATA boundaries, true duplicate outer identity, missing/duplicate subclass rejection, corrected same-facade retries, and conservative namespace status. Direct observation separately tests nested subtype and trailing XDATA scope precedence.

limitations: The previously existing typed and raw SORTENTSTABLE readers already avoid registering subclass sort keys as self identities; this change only refines physical observation.

SortOrder remains unqualified by the namespace audit. AC1018 adapter namespace capture remains gated; this evidence does not establish ownership, target resolution, document output or native semantic support.
The append-only public enum preserves existing numeric values and representation; downstream exhaustive switches must handle the new scope conservatively. Rebuild consumers of the changed header.
